scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 3 with Figures 4-7, Tables A1-A2 and Figures A1-A2 (Section 3 simulation experiment)
scenario.description: FloTHERM transient simulation of an IGBT module on a cold plate with a 50 um TIM layer, for TIM conductivities of 0.2, 1 and 4 W/mK. The left IGBT chip (11.2 mm x 11.2 mm) is powered. Monitor points Ch0-Ch4 are the junction, TIM top and bottom, and points displaced 3 mm. The paper reports Zth curves, structure functions and RthJC/RthJA (RthJA = 0.52, 0.36 and 0.28 K/W). The text gives a 100 W step, while the Figure 4 caption says 50 W.
scenario.architecture: Single powered IGBT chip in a power module: silicon, die attach, copper, AlN ceramic, copper, solder, aluminum base plate, thermal grease, aluminum cold plate. Cold plate modelled with a constant HTC of 3000 W/m2K. Stack layer sizes are in Table A2 (pdf page 26).
scenario.workload: Uniform power step (heating) on the die surface. Text states 100 W, Figure 4 caption states 50 W.
scenario.operating_point: TIM 50 um thick with 0.2, 1 or 4 W/mK conductivity; cold plate HTC 3000 W/m2K; steady state reached at about 140 s, 50 s and 30 s respectively. Observable: junction temperature Ch0 (die top center) transient and Zth(t) = dTJ/P in K/W, giving RthJC and RthJA.

original_setup.solver: FloTHERM (Mentor/Siemens) transient 3D finite-volume thermal simulation of an IGBT module on a cold plate, as cited on pdf pages 5 and 28. Mesh, time stepping and ambient temperature are not given.
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper reports a simulation experiment, not an optimization or placement study.
original_setup.controller: None. A single uniform power step is applied to the powered left IGBT die, and the cold plate has a constant HTC of 3000 W/m2K (pdf page 5).
original_setup.benchmark: Section 3 simulation experiment (pdf pages 4-11, Figures 3-10, Tables A1-A2, Figures A1-A2). The module has an 11.2 mm x 11.2 mm IGBT die on a Si/die attach/Cu/AlN/Cu/solder/Al base plate stack with a 50 um TIM layer. The TIM conductivity is 0.2, 1 or 4 W/mK. The paper reports Zth(t), structure functions, RthJC and RthJA (0.52, 0.36 and 0.28 K/W).

thermal_observable.location: RthJA (junction to ambient) from the Ch0 junction temperature, taken at the center of the powered die top (dissipating layer). The value is for the 0.2 W/mK TIM case; the paper gives 0.36 K/W for 1 W/mK and 0.28 K/W for 4 W/mK.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Steady-state endpoint of the single-point transient Zth(t) = dTJ(t)/P, in K/W. It is not a spatial average and not a die maximum. Steady state is reached at about 140 s, 50 s and 30 s for the three TIM cases.

physical_mismatches.reason: The scenario is a transient 3D multilayer power module (die, die attach, Cu, AlN, Cu, solder, Al base plate, TIM, Al cold plate). It is not a 2.5D chiplet system with an interposer, so a steady 2D chiplet floorplan model cannot represent it.

The paper's observable is the transient junction response and the steady RthJA at a single die-center point of a 3D vertical heat path. Lateral spreading in the thick base plate and cold plate, and the cold-plate HTC boundary, are essential to it. A 2D planar model drops these.
The cooling boundary is a constant HTC of 3000 W/m2K on the cold plate, with a TIM layer of 0.2, 1 or 4 W/mK. Studio's cooling model may differ.

The power step is inconsistent in the paper: the text says 100 W (pdf page 5) and the Figure 4 caption says 50 W (pdf page 6). Zth and RthJA are normalized by power, so a power trace cannot be set unambiguously.
The scenario has no optimizer, controller, reliability analysis or placement. These elements cannot be compared or reproduced.
The study concerns measurement methodology: monitor-point displacement, TDIM structure functions and RthJC divergence thresholds. These do not map to a steady-state per-block temperature output.

studio_assumptions: No Studio package or material assumptions are supplied in the packet, so none are recorded. No floorplan is generated.
The packet does not give complete placed block coordinates, so the floorplan is left empty. No illustrative 2D placement is constructed.
Any Studio result for this paper should not be compared numerically to RthJA = 0.52 K/W, because the scenario is 3D, transient and multilayer.
missing_inputs: No pinned packet assets are supplied (assets list is empty), so there is no config, geometry file, power file or code.

Placement is missing: there are no x_m, y_m coordinates for the powered IGBT die, the second IGBT or other chips. Figure A1 is only a sketch, and Table A2 gives only stack sizes (die 11.2 x 11.2 x 0.3 mm).
The number and dimensions of the other chips in the module are not given.
Power is ambiguous: the text says 100 W and the Figure 4 caption says 50 W. No power time series is published beyond a step, and no rule is given for splitting power among blocks.
Ambient or cold-plate fluid temperature, FloTHERM mesh and solver settings, and the time step are not given.
The Table A2 caption refers to Section 4 while the data belong to the Section 3 simulation, so the scenario-to-table mapping needs verification.
The paper-linked URLs on pdf page 28 (FloTHERM, T3Ster, standards, datasheets) are references and tool pages. None of them proves that simulation inputs or models exist.
The 0.52, 0.36 and 0.28 K/W values are given in the text. The Zth curves and structure functions are figures only and would need digitization with stated uncertainty.

assessment.summary: Verdict: not_2d_applicable. The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status skipped; simulation_allowed false; comparison_valid false). The selected scenario is the Section 3 FloTHERM transient simulation of a single powered 11.2 mm x 11.2 mm x 0.3 mm IGBT die in a 3D multilayer power module (Si, die attach, Cu, AlN, Cu, solder, Al base plate, 50 um TIM, Al cold plate with constant HTC 3000 W/m2K). The paper reports RthJA of 0.52, 0.36 and 0.28 K/W for TIM conductivities of 0.2, 1 and 4 W/mK. These are single-point (die-top center, Ch0) steady-state endpoints of a transient Zth(t) curve. The extracted experiment is custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power_w, so the input gate failed ('A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object'). The scientific gate also failed, and nothing was independently verified. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation or a pinned Ascend910/ATPlace case, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated, and no source commit or generated-placement assumption applies. No placement was invented because the paper gives no x/y coordinates (Figure A1 is only a sketch). Even if Studio had run, a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace, so it could not be compared to the transient Zth response. Because the location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions do not match, no numerical comparison to 0.52, 0.36 or 0.28 K/W is made. Qualitatively, the paper shows that a better TIM lowers RthJA and shortens the time to steady state (about 140 s, 50 s and 30 s). A steady 2D model could at most indicate the same direction of sensitivity to vertical resistance, and only as a hypothesis, not as replication. The final verdict is fixed by the deterministic gate, and this result is not an exact replication.
limitations: Gate outcome: not_2d_applicable, so simulation was skipped and comparison_valid is false; no Studio temperatures exist to compare.
Regime mismatch: the paper observable is a transient Zth(t) and its steady endpoint, while a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace.
Geometry mismatch: the scenario is a 3D multilayer power module with lateral spreading in a base plate and cold plate, not a 2.5D chiplet floorplan; a planar 2D model drops these essential effects.
Location and aggregation mismatch: the paper value is a single die-top-center point (Ch0), not a spatial average or die maximum, so it cannot be matched to a per-block Studio output.

Boundary mismatch: the original uses a constant cold-plate HTC of 3000 W/m2K with a 50 um TIM of 0.2, 1 or 4 W/mK; Studio's cooling and material model may differ and no Studio assumptions were supplied.
Power ambiguity: the text states 100 W and the Figure 4 caption states 50 W; no power trace or splitting rule is given.
Missing inputs: no pinned assets, no chip placement coordinates, unknown number and size of other chips, and no ambient temperature, mesh or time step for FloTHERM.
The Table A2 caption refers to Section 4, so the mapping of the stack table to the Section 3 simulation is inferred; evidence 21 also lacks a valid page or pinned asset locator.
